content: Meu nome é Nathan. Sou um desenvolvedor e roteirista de jogos morando no Brasil. Publico meus jogos sob o pseudonimo de N. Erebus. Meu objetivo é criar experiências únicas e memoráveis que fiquem com o jogador muito após o seu fim.

Engine: Godot 4 Posição: Desenvolvedor solo Tempo de gameplay: 10-15 minutos Plataformas: Windows
Description#A surreal 3D first-person platformer inspired by FLCL, Twin Peaks, Alice in Wonderland, and a little bit of Radiohead. It follows a powerful child who must bring joy to the villagers of the Village at the Edge of the Universe, so that they can call up their dormant god to take them away.
Design Goals#This game was designed to be played and finished in one sitting while still sticking with the player long after they closed it. To do that, I tried to surprise the player on every section, making sure they could never guess what was coming next.
Challenges#As with my last project, this was also for a game jam. I had eight days to build it, and planned my time accordingly with a buffer period in case something happened. And something did happen. I had a really bad migraine that cost me one day of potential progress. I considered removing one of the later platforming sections to focus on polishing the rest of the game, but after thinking really hard, I realized that removing it would diminish the effect of the ending because of the pacing. In the end, I choose to work really hard on the last few days to make sure that the section in question made the cut.

title: Gire Comigo no Fim do Universo

Engine: Godot 4 Posição: Desenvolvedor solo ** Tempo de gameplay: ~5 minutos Plataformas: Navegador, Windows
Description#This game tells the story of a young boy named Marco and his obsession with attention. It uses gameplay, level design, and sound design to tell that story effectively in a way that matches the protagonist’s personal journey. It was originally written in Brazilian Portuguese, but I later localized it to English.
Design Goals#I wanted to connect narrative and gameplay to enhance the effect of both, creating something that is greater than the sum of its parts.
Challenges#This project was a game jam project, and I had two other people working with me at the start. They had to leave, however, due to personal reasons after the brainstorming phase, meaning I had to do everything else by myself. This meant reducing the scope, and changing the art style to something simpler while keeping the tone and effect intact.

content:
Johnny was an unremarkable baby born at the age of zero to even more unremarkable parents. He learned to speak early and seemed very happy about it, his parents, not so much.
Johnny spoke of space and aliens, of robots and spaceships. He asked all the question a child of his age should ask and a little bit more. His mother tried her best to answer, and invented what she couldn’t. His father didn’t bother. Johnny suspected that the adults didn’t know as much as he thought.
All that curiosity paid off in school. His grades were good, and the teachers spoke well of him. Maths and sciences were his favourites. He would ask the teachers many questions about space, and they would always answer with the same flat tone: “That won’t be on the test, so no need to bother you silly little head with that.”
At the age of 13, he met a girl. His grades dropped, but not by much. He wasn’t brave enough to confess, but the idea of seeing her was motivation enough to keep studying hard. Luckily for Johnny, the girl was into smart boys. She would be the one to make the move just before high school.
Graduation was in sight, and university life was next. But Johnny hadn’t decided on a career path yet. He had too many interests, how could he possibly choose one? “Choose an easy field that pays well, but just enough.” His father said. “Don’t dream too big. You’re smart. Only fools dream big.” During the final days before graduation, the school distributed pamphlets containing a list of career paths in alphabetical order with a heavy focus on how well they pay and how difficult they are to get into. His girlfriend chose journalism, and he chose the architecture because it was the first item of the list.
Many years later, he had married his school sweetheart and had two children. He had a job that paid well, and he was decent at it. Not the best, but the most reliable. Most of the buildings in the big city were his, the small ones and the big ones. They all looked the same though. When colleagues questioned his style choice, he would always say: “I just do what the clients tell me to do.”
Middle age brought some bad news. Cancer, his doctor said, terminal, in fact. There was nothing he could do except to wait for the inevitable. He looked back to all his life achievements only to find a shelf with worthless awards and certificates. His friends and colleagues all became the best while he was only “reliable”.
One last client came to him before he closed up shop. Some rich businessman wanting a building as large as his ego. Johnny didn’t care about who he was, but was willing to do the job. He didn’t care much about anything at this point. He just wanted to make something good, and this was his last job. Johnny agreed saying: “I’ll make you a building that will touch the stars.”
That building would be known as “the star-scrapper”, and it was indeed his greatest work. His only good work some would say. But Johnny didn’t care. He had finally made something he was proud of, and that seemed to be enough for him.
It was finally time to close down his office. He took all the important stuff in a cardboard box including the space themed miniatures he received from friends and family. As he left the building, he was amazed by how beautiful the full moon looked. And just to the right of it, silhouetted against the moonlight, was the star-scraper doing what it was made to do. Johnny looked at it one last time, and a tear escaped from his eye. The building looked just like a rocket ready to launch into the unknown.
Notas de tradução
O texto foi originalmente escrito em inglês. Decidi mudar o nome do protagonista de “Jonny Mann” para “João Costa” para manter a ideia de um homem comum com um nome ainda mais comum.
title: A Vida Medíocre de João Costa

content:
Warning: This story contains very graphic depictions of gore and violence
“I don’t like your eyes”. The old man says before leaping on top of the boy. His knees become shackles for the kid’s arms. The boy screams and jerks trying to get out, but there’s no one around to hear him.
The old man brings his dirty fingers near the boy’s eyes, tapping it and using his crooked fingernails to gain purchase. Blood and tears cover the boy’s face.
“Help! Help! He’s pulling my eye out!” The boy screams, but no one is there to hear.
The right eye pops out of the skull, dangling only by the nerves. The man grins joyfully and uses his teeth to cut it off completely. The boy screams, and the old man screams back in his face.
“Now to the other one.” The eyeball rolls over the grass.
The boy tries to fight back as much as he can, but the old man’s strength is too much for him. He passes out from shock and pain. The man frows at the lack of resistance.
“What are you doing to my baby!” Screams the woman on the distance.
The sound of the mother’s shriek pierces the old man’s ear.
He raises both of his bloody hands into the air and gets up slowly while shaking his head. Satisfied, he steps on the eye with his worker boots and walks away as if nothing had happened. The mother sprints towards her unconscious child while the man disappears into the forest.
title: Eu Não Gosto Dos Teus Olhos

content:
In a weapon store illuminated only by the sun outside and just a few candles hanging on the walls, the always smiling store owner greets a party of three that had just entered the store.
“Welcome, welcome! Make yourself at home. But don’t be too comfortable, things aren’t free.” He says gesturing to his merchandise.
“What are you guys getting? I don’t think there’s anything for me here.” Asks Mirah, the elf mage.
“A bow.” Says Keth, the quiet rogue in the back.
“A bow? You can’t use a bow, can you?” Says Terrick, the leader of the party.
“I am willing to learn. Besides, We’ve been too reliant on Mirah. What if she’s unable to cast her spells?”
“Easy, I’ll protect her.”
“That’s not the point, but I like your enthusiasm.”
“I agree…” Mirah says, slightly embarrassed.
“Well, you do what you think is best. You are our brain after all”. Terrick spots a display case. It’s not unlike the others, but he’s compelled to walk to it.
“You know those stories where the blade chooses their wielders? I think this one chose me.” He grabs the sword and gives a few swings. “I’m taking it.”
“I don’t think this is a good idea.”. Mirah grabs the sword herself, and struggles a little with the weight. She holds it upside down to inspect the handle.
“Why?”
Keth approaches holding a hunting bow and a quiver. “Oh, a dark blade. These things are hard to come by.”
“I think it’s cursed.” Mirah adds.
“Cursed?! This isn’t cursed! Is this sword cursed, mister?”
“No.” The store owner responds still smiling.
“See?”
“Just look at it! There’s a skull on the pommel!” Mirah brings the pommel to Terrick’s face.
“That could mean anything. I bet it’s a stylistic choice.” Terrick grabs the sword back, and as he does, the mood shifts.
The light are sucked out of the sky, and the world outside turns into nothingness. The flames on the candles hanging on the walls begin to dance in anticipation. The distant sound of footsteps travel through the air and into their frightened ears, closer and closer, until it reaches the front door.
“Welcome, welcome!” The store owner hides behind the counter. “Make yourself at home. But don’t be too comfortable, things aren’t free.”
“I don’t think he’s a client.” Terrick hides the sword behind his back.
The door opens by itself revealing a slender hooded man. His head almost hits the tall ceiling when he enters. He looks around for a long moment, taking special interest on the collection of swords. Mirah slowly moves behind. The figure takes notice of her staff and whispers something no one can hear. Pulling off his hood, he reveals his skeleton face.
“My sword… It’s here…”
“It’s a warlock, Terrick. Give the sword to him…” Mirah whispers.
“Not a chance. Can’t you use one of your spells?”
Mirah does a gesture with her hands, but nothing happens.
“I can’t”
“Why?”
“I think he’s blocking my magic.”
“He can do that? How’s that fair? Is there anything you can do?”
“Not while he’s holding the spell. I need a distraction.”
“Well, stay behind me then.” He looks around. “Where is Keth?”
“I’ll kill every one here if I don’t get my sword back.” The warlock turns towards the two. “You!” Mirah gets closer to Terrick. “What are the two of you whispering about? You wouldn’t happen to have my sword, would you?” Terrick shakes his head. The warlock laughs. “What’s that behind your back, then?”
Terrick turns his head to look at the sword, but the frightened face of his friend catches his eyes first. She does her best to hide it, but he sees right through her. Still hiding the sword, he sighs, taking a step forward, then another, until he is face to face with the tall skeleton. He raises his head, and looks deep into the warlock’s eyes.
“This is a weapon store, mate. If you want a sword, you’ll have to pay like all others.”
The skeleton is furious. “Don’t you dare mock me!” He shouts raising his hand and holding the air in front of him. Terrick floats and chokes, but refuses to drop the sword. As his face turns blue, all Mirah can do is watch.
With teary eyes, she holds her staff in front of her, but the skeleton instantly turns his head towards her, and, using the few muscles left on his face, grins maliciously. Mirah shuts her eyes. “Keth, where are you?” She mumbles to herself.
It’s when all hope seem lost that she hears the sound of an arrow flying. She opens her eyes, and sees the warlock looking out of the window, then to a pile of wooden boxes that weren’t there before. This is the opportunity she was waiting for.
While the skeleton is distracted looking for the shooter, the elf girl quickly aims the staff, and whispers. A small pebble comes out of the tip of the staff, growing larger and larger as it flies out, turning into a small boulder. It hits the skeleton on his head, breaking his neck. He cracks it back into place. The spell did some damage, but not enough. But, it was enough to make him release Terrick, who stood ready with the sword in his hands.
Terrick lunges. The sword makes contact with the warlock’s sternum, going through without any resistance. They both look equally confused. The momentum makes them both fall. The skeleton, shocked, looks at Terrick and opens his jaw to speak.
“I misjudged you… You are… Worthy… My sword is yours.”
The light comes back to the sky and back into the room, illuminating the skeleton as it turns to dust. Covered with the remains of his opponent, Terrick stands up victorious.
“We did it! We actually did it! I can’t believe it.” Mirah runs up to Terrick and gives him a big hug. “Oh…” And accidentally covers herself with the dust.
“Sorry about that.” Terrick says.
“That was reckless. Why did you do that?” She punches him on the shoulder.
“Ouch! Because I trusted you, like I always do. That and I wanted to keep the sword.”
Keth comes out of hiding and walks up to them. “Huh, guess I need more practice. I’m not joining on the group hug this time, I rather remain clean, but you have my praise. That was impressive. Especially you, Mirah.”
“I assume the curse is lifted then. Ugh, I hope I get a discount.” Terrick says looking at his weapon.
They catch their breath and walk to the counter. The store owner comes out of hiding. “Is he finally gone? Truly Gone?”
“I would hope so, he turned to dust. Sorry about the mess, by the way.” Terrick responds.
“And did I hear that right? He called you worthy, didn’t he?”
“Well, yes. He saw how skilled I am. Though I don’t like to brag.” He says braggingly.
“Then, I have something for you.” he pulls out a large wooden box and opens it. There’s a plain looking sword inside it.
“What’s this?”
“It’s a sword. A cursed sword. Only the one deemed worthy by its previous owner can wield it, and since he called you worthy, you can have it.”
“But…”
“I never expected him to actually come back for it. Especially after being dead for over 20 years.”
“But… What about this one?”
“This one?” He inspects the dark blade. “This is just a ceremonial sword. It’s useless for fighting. I’ve been trying to get rid of it for a long time, but everyone assumes that it’s cursed. You can have it as well if you want.” He hands the sword back.
“But there’s a skull on the pommel!” Terrick exclaims. Mirah raises her eyebrow.
“It’s a stylistic choice.”
“Of course it is.”
title: A Espada Amaldiçoada
